column1: # dd-zero-family.tsv -- WHICH FAMILY each baseline row belongs to.
# TAB-separated, exactly one tab per line.
# The point is to answer "is this site in any row?" MECHANICALLY.  dd-mut-proof.py
# answers "is this site reachable?" by renaming the def; this answers the other
# half -- "if it IS reachable, does the READER print it?" -- which is the
# distinction between PORT-DEFECT and INVISIBLE-to-reader.
# The families are read off the GATE's own structure in the frozen snapshot:
#   l2idt*, f2fdt*   dd_text.head -> dd_l2i.row / dd_f2f.row   (dtype.py:12, :97)
#   lg*, hi42*       l2i.rows / l2i.hi42                      (dtype.py:21-81)
#   up*              unpack.one -> unpack32                    (dtype.py:13)
#   c*               dd_cmx.rows -> f2f_clamp_max              (dtype.py:139)
# `l2i` is deliberately COARSE: every `lg*` row is a `l2i` arm, and the fine
# attribution -- which arm reads which site -- is what the per-mutation MOVED row
# lists already record.  Coarse here means "a site inside l2i is visible to the
# l2i family", which is the CONSERVATIVE direction: it can only under-report
# INVISIBLE-to-reader, never invent one.  zero-classify.py's `inside()` treats
# `l2i_shl.hi` as inside `l2i` by the dotted prefix, so one line covers the tree.
^l2idt\d
^f2fdt\d
^lg
^hi42
^up
^c\d
